source_text:
Ἐπεὶ δὲ
ἤκουσα ὅτι τινὲς ἐγόγγυσαν καθ' ἡμῶν, ὅτι ἐν τῷ διαβαίνειν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸν ἅγιον
τόπον τῆς Βεθῆλ τοῦ συναγελασθῆναι τῇ σῇ τιμιότητι ὡς ἤλθομεν εἰς τὴν κώμην
τὴν λεγομένην Ἀναυθά, θεασάμενοι λύχνον καιόμενον καὶ ἐρωτήσαντες ἔγνωμεν
ἐκκλησίαν εἶναι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ, εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ τοῦ εὐχὴν ἐπιτελέσαι εὕρομεν βῆλον
ἐν τῇ θύρᾳ βαπτὸν ἐν ᾧ ἐζωγράφητο ἀνδροείκελόν τι εἰδωλοειδές, ὃ ἔλεγον τάχα ὅτι

Χριστοῦ ἦν τὸ ἐκτύπωμα ἢ ἑνὸς τῶν ἁγίων οὐ γὰρ μέμνημαι ἐγὼ θεασάμενος, καὶ
εἰδὼς ὅτι μύσος ἐστὶν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ τοιαῦτα εἶναι, διέρρηξα αὐτὸ καὶ συνεβούλευσα
ἀμφιάσαι ἐν αὐτῷ πένητα τελευτήσαντα, οἱ δὲ γογγύσαντες ἔλεγον· "ἔδει αὐτὸν
ἀλλάξαι ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων τὸ βῆλον πρινὴ αὐτὸ σχίσῃ", καίτοιγε ἐμοῦ ὑποσχομένου ὅτι
ἀντ' αὐτοῦ ἀπο 283 στελῶ ἕτερον, ἐβράδυνα δὲ τοῦ ἀποστεῖλαι διὰ τὸ ἀναγκαῖόν με
thought_title: Tearing the painted curtain at Anautha
orientation: Epiphanius tells John what happened when he entered a church at Anautha while traveling to meet John at Bethel.
pass_a_gloss: But since I heard that some grumbled against us, that while we were passing through to the holy place of Bethel to meet with your honor, when we came to the village called Anautha, having seen a lamp burning and having asked we learned that there is a church in the place, and entering to fulfill a prayer we found a curtain in the door, dyed, in which there had been painted some human image, idol-like, which they were saying perhaps was a likeness of Christ or of one of the saints, for I myself when I saw it do not remember, and knowing that it is an abomination for such things to be in a church, I tore it apart and I advised to wrap in it a poor man who had died, and the ones who grumbled were saying: "He ought to have replaced the curtain from his own means before he tore it," although I was promising that in place of it I will send another, but I was slow to send because of the necessity for me [sentence breaks off].

choices.why: brief fixes τιμιότης as honor as title of address
brief fixes both key terms; τι keeps indefinite force

choices.term: μύσος ἐστὶν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ τοιαῦτα εἶναι
choices.english: it is an abomination for such things to be in a church
choices.why: brief fixes μύσος and ἐκκλησία; keeps infinitive construction
rejected: it is a defilement for such things to be in the assembly

choices.term: ἔδει αὐτὸν ἀλλάξαι ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων τὸ βῆλον πρινὴ αὐτὸ σχίσῃ
choices.english: he ought to have replaced the curtain from his own means before he tore it
choices.why: keeps past obligation with aorist infinitive, source of replacement, and temporal before clause
rejected: he should change the veil at his own expense before rending it

pass_b_english: But I heard that some grumbled against us. While we were traveling on to the holy place at Bethel to meet with your honor, we came to the village called Anautha. I saw a lamp burning, and when I asked I learned that there was a church in that place. I went in to pray, and I found a dyed curtain on the door, painted with some human image, idol-like. They said it was perhaps a likeness of Christ or of one of the saints, for I myself, though I saw it, do not remember whose image it was.

Knowing that it is an abomination for such things to be in a church, I tore it and advised wrapping a poor dead person in it. But those who grumbled said, “He ought to have replaced the curtain from his own means before he tore it,” although I had promised to send another in its place. I was slow to send it because pressing need held me.
notes: Printed text reads ἀπο 283 στελῶ, with 283 intruded page number; read as ἀποστελῶ. Final clause διὰ τὸ ἀναγκαῖόν με breaks off and continues in the next section.

problems.quote: though I myself do not remember seeing it
problems.why: The Greek means he saw it but does not recall whose image it was, which is why he relies on what they said. The English says he does not remember seeing it, contradicting the narrative.
problems.fix: for, though I saw it, I do not remember clearly whose image it was.
problems.ruling: After εὕρομεν and ἐζωγραφήτο, οὐ μέμνημαι with θεασάμενος denies recalling whose likeness, not having seen it.

edits.old: though I myself do not remember seeing it.
edits.new: for I myself, though I saw it, do not remember whose image it was.

fixed: Fixed `though I myself do not remember seeing it': source οὐ γὰρ μέμνημαι ἐγὼ θεασάμενος explains reliance on ὃ ἔλεγον; he found and tore the curtain, so he saw it but does not recall whose likeness it bore.
